title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 735-737 of the Longue Marche sequel): Grothendieck is testing the section conjecture on the Fermat covers U_n of U = P^1_Q - {0,1,infinity}. These are the Kummer covers with group (M/nM)(1), where M-hat = Z-hat(1)^{0,1,inf}/Z-hat(1) is the abelianized geometric fundamental group of U. He works with the 'abelian' (more precisely mod-n abelian) approximation of pi_1. On the previous page he showed two things. First, M-hat[n]-conjugacy classes of splittings determine the corresponding rational point x_n up to gamma_n = mu_n(Q)^{0,1,inf}/mu_n(Q), which is trivial for n odd. Second, the possible classes of splittings are classified by (379): H^1(Gamma_Q, M-hat) = (Q^*)^ (Kummer) tensored with M, which is isomorphic to G(Q)^.

This page names G := G_m^{0,1,inf}/G_m (diagonal G_m). This is the 2-dimensional split torus whose character group is the degree-0 divisors supported on {0,1,inf}. In modern terms it is the generalized Jacobian (Albanese) of U, i.e. the open torus of P^2 complementary to the coordinate triangle. The U_n embed in it as Fermat curves: they are the pull-back of U under the n-th power isogeny of G, sitting inside G as the Fermat curve minus its points on the triangle.

The point Grothendieck makes: at this level of approximation, H^1(Gamma_Q, M-hat) is just the profinite Kummer completion of G(Q). So studying the existence and cohomological location of sections amounts to studying rational points of the torus G itself. The equation cutting U_n out of G plays no role. The approximation is therefore far too coarse: it is purely 'abelian' analysis, i.e. Kummer theory for the Albanese torus. Finer, non-abelian (nilpotent / metabelian) approximations are needed.

The next page accordingly begins §2, 'Enveloppes schématiques des L-groupes', the machinery for such finer approximations.
errors: The equation as transcribed, x_0^n + x_1^n + x_inf^n = 1, is not homogeneous, so it is not well defined on G = G_m^3/G_m. Presumably intended: the homogeneous Fermat equation (x_0^n + x_1^n + x_inf^n = 0, with suitable signs), or the affine normalization x_0^n + x_1^n = 1. This is a notational slip, not a mathematical error.

Not an error, but an imprecision: the identification 'sections up to conjugacy = G(Q)^' only parametrizes candidate cohomology classes of splittings at the abelian level. Grothendieck's own conclusion, that this level contains no information about U_n, is correct.

ideas.what: Classes of sections of the abelianized (or mod-n abelianized) fundamental extension of P^1-{0,1,inf} are given by Kummer theory, H^1(Gamma_Q, M-hat) = G(Q)^, where G is the generalized Jacobian torus
ideas.modern_name: Abelian section conjecture / Kummer map for the Albanese (generalized Jacobian) of a hyperbolic curve
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; treated systematically in Stix's work on the section conjecture (2000s-2010s) and in Ellenberg's and Wickelgren's analyses of P^1-{0,1,inf}
ideas.where_published: Not in the 1983 Faltings letter or the Esquisse in this explicit form, as far as I know; unsure

ideas.what: Fermat curves embedded in the 2-dimensional torus G_m^3/G_m as the pull-back of U under the n-th power isogeny
ideas.modern_name: Fermat curves as Kummer/abelian covers of P^1-{0,1,inf} via the generalized Jacobian
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; Ihara (1986) and Anderson on Galois action on Fermat curves

ideas.what: Recognition that abelian approximations of pi_1 carry no Diophantine information on the covers (the equation of U_n is invisible), so nilpotent/non-abelian refinements are necessary
ideas.modern_name: Need for higher (2-nilpotent, metabelian) obstructions in the section conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ellenberg (2-nilpotent obstruction, c. 2000), Wickelgren, Kim (unipotent/nonabelian Chabauty), Stix

missed.claim: Historical: Grothendieck explicitly diagnosed, in the 1980s, that the abelian level of the section-conjecture analysis for Fermat covers reduces to Kummer theory of the torus G_m^3/G_m. He concluded that finer non-abelian approximations are needed, which motivates his 'schematic envelopes of L-groups'. This anticipates the later programme of nilpotent obstructions (Ellenberg, Wickelgren, Kim), but the mathematical content itself is standard.
missed.quote: tout se passe comme si on étudiait simplement l'existence (!) et le repérage cohomologique des pts Q-rationnels de G lui-même - sans se préoccuper de l'équation ... qui définit U_n
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority for the motivation (abelian approximation is useless, go nilpotent/schematic), not a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a short, correct but routine observation: the abelian level reduces to Kummer theory of the Albanese torus. It mainly serves as motivation for the next section. Its historical interest is the early explicit recognition of the need for non-abelian approximations, a view later developed by others.
transcription_corrections: 'les F_n' should read 'les U_n' (the image shows 'Un'); likewise 'qui définit U_n'.
'repérage' is plausible (image: 'repérage'), 'cohomologiques des pts Q-rationnels de G'.
'Cela montre à l'évidence que l'approximation ...' rather than 'Cela montre : l'évidence que'.
'Je ne dirai' is likely 'Je ne crois pas'/'Il est clair' (uncertain); the sense is 'qu'il est nécessaire de passer à des approximations plus fines' ('des' should read 'à des').
